bounds.rationale: Two keeps the double-terminal-entry state REPRESENTABLE, so TerminalEnteredAtMostOnce fails loudly under its declared mutation instead of being true by typing.

invariants.name: TypeInvariant
invariants.statement: Every variable stays inside its declared finite domain: the four ready states, the close-code domain, the two reason classes, the inbound and outbound vocabularies, and the bounded terminal-entry counter.
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.type-domain-escape -- set Init's closeDetail code to 9999, outside CloseCodeDomain.

invariants.name: TerminalEnteredAtMostOnce
invariants.statement: The absorbing terminal state is entered at most once. The counter's domain deliberately allows two, so the double-entry state is representable and this check is falsifiable rather than true by typing.
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.double-terminal-entry -- add "Closed" to TransportEof's enabling state set.

invariants.name: ClosedIffOneTerminalEntry
invariants.statement: Reaching the terminal state and accounting for it are the same event: no path enters Closed without the terminal accounting, and no accounting happens without Closed.
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.terminal-entry-unaccounted -- in RecvCloseWhileClosing replace the terminal-entry increment with UNCHANGED.

invariants.name: CloseDetailPresentFromClosing
invariants.statement: From CLOSING onward a governing close outcome exists: every modeled path into CLOSING or CLOSED records the origin and code that the terminal delivery later reports.
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.closing-without-detail -- in SendCloseAccepted replace the closeDetail assignment with UNCHANGED.

invariants.name: InboundCloseNormalization
invariants.statement: The shipped inbound close-payload table, restated independently of the receive actions: empty accepts as 1000, one octet accepts as 1002 (behavior-delta sequence 27, where the RFC would treat it as malformed), a valid code plus reason accepts, 1007 with an empty reason rejects as 1007, a reserved or out-of-range code rejects as 1002, and an invalid UTF-8 reason is a runtime rejection with NO reported close code (behavior-delta sequence 32).
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.one-byte-rejected -- change InboundCode's one_byte arm to 1005, which the validity chain then rejects, turning the accept row into an invalid_data row.

invariants.name: EchoCarriesConstructorPayload
invariants.statement: The echoed close frame always carries the CONSTRUCTOR payload, whose wire code is 1000, regardless of the received code (behavior-delta sequence 28). This is the invariant that would have caught an RFC-shaped acknowledgement echo.
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.echo-mirrors-received-code -- in RecvCloseAcceptOpen set the echo's payload to code_reason and its code to the received code.

invariants.name: ForbiddenCodesNeverReachTheWire
invariants.statement: No close code that the shipped validity chain forbids ever reaches the wire, for either the local close path (checked against its requested reason) or the echo path (checked against the constructor's empty reason).
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.validity-chain-bypassed -- delete the CloseCodeRejection guard from SendCloseAccepted.

invariants.name: TlsErrorSendAlwaysRejectedAs1002
invariants.statement: A local close requesting the TLS_ERROR code 1015 is ALWAYS rejected with reported code 1002, for every reason kind. This is the mechanical statement of the recorded inert-normalization finding.
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.tls-error-sendable -- delete the 1015 arm from the validity chain's fourth clause AND drop the normalization from SendCloseAccepted.

invariants.name: NeverConnectedOnlyPreHandshake
invariants.statement: The NEVER_CONNECTED code is a callback-vocabulary code, never a wire code, and can only be reported before the handshake completed.
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.never-connected-post-handshake -- in TransportEof's abnormal arm report the never-connected code instead of 1006.

invariants.name: RejectedSendDoesNotTransition
invariants.statement: A rejected local close emits no frame and does not move the lifecycle: the typed failure is reported to the caller and the connection poisons in place. This is the recorded, declared divergence from shipped Java's close(), which enters CLOSING on an illegal code.

invariants.name: PoisonNeverFabricatesTermination
invariants.statement: The fatal-poison flag and the terminal state are independent absorbing facts: poisoning outside the terminal state never fabricates a terminal entry.
invariants.falsified_by: defect.close.poison-implies-closed -- add a terminal-entry increment to RecvCloseRejectedOpen.

properties.name: TerminalAbsorbing
properties.statement: CLOSED is absorbing: no modeled transition leaves the terminal state.
properties.falsified_by: defect.close.reopen-after-terminal -- add a Reopen action from Closed to Open.

properties.name: PoisonAbsorbing
properties.statement: The fatal-poison flag is absorbing and freezes the lifecycle: once a fatal typed failure is reported, no further input changes the state or the governing close outcome.
properties.falsified_by: defect.close.poison-recoverable -- drop the not-poisoned conjunct from OpenHandshake and TransportEof.

properties.name: ClosingResolves
properties.statement: Under the declared fairness, a closing connection that has not suffered a fatal failure always terminates; a poisoned one is allowed to stop, because the kernel's contract is to report and freeze and leave transport teardown to the adapter.
properties.falsified_by: defect.close.starved-closing-resolution -- change the cfg SPECIFICATION from FairSpec to Spec.

findings.statement: The port's send-path normalization of the TLS_ERROR code 1015 to 1005 omits Java's accompanying side effect: shipped CloseFrame.setCode also clears the reason (framing/CloseFrame.java:184), and the port's pure normalizer does not. TLC shows the difference is observationally INERT on this path: TlsErrorSendAlwaysRejectedAs1002 holds over both reason kinds, because 1005 with a non-empty reason is rejected 1002 by the chain's second arm, 1005 with an empty reason is rejected 1002 by the fourth, and an un-normalized 1015 is rejected 1002 by the fourth as well. Every route reports 1002 and emits no frame, so the port's observable behavior matches the fidelity authority. No change is required; the difference is recorded so a future refactor cannot silently rely on it.

Shipped Java's close(code, message, remote) catches the InvalidDataException raised by the close frame's isValid, calls flushAndClose with the abnormal-close code, and then sets readyState = CLOSING (WebSocketImpl.java:488-503) -- so a Java endpoint ENTERS CLOSING on an illegal local close code. The port's Sans-I/O kernel instead returns the typed failure to the caller, emits no frame, and does not transition, matching the reference model internal/corpora/derive.go sendClose, which the US-016 owner amendment names as the binding fidelity authority. The invariant RejectedSendDoesNotTransition pins the port's behavior, and the difference from raw Java is recorded here rather than hidden. It lives in the adapter layer's scope (US-018), not the kernel's; it is NOT covered by an existing behavior-delta-ledger record, so an owner decision on whether it warrants one is the honest next step.

honesty_notes: Claim ceiling proved-model, full stop. This run establishes properties of an ABSTRACTION of the shipped connection kernel and nothing about production Rust without a reviewed composition/refinement link.

The model is bounded and abstract: eight representative send codes, two reason classes, six inbound payload classes, and no queue, event-budget, or backpressure modelling. Checked results hold only inside those bounds.

This model checks the PORT's Sans-I/O kernel, not shipped Java. The US-006 connection model (assurance/formal/connection-model.tla) models Java's lifecycle, including its at-least-once terminal callback under listener re-entrancy. Neither model subsumes the other, and the terminal discipline checked here -- one entry into the absorbing Closed state -- is NOT the same claim as Java's callback count.
OWNER_ATTESTED_NOT_INDEPENDENT: one session authored the model, the invariants, the falsification notes, and this record, and ran the checker. No independent review is claimed.

Non-vacuity is partial, stated precisely: two of the eleven invariants (EchoCarriesConstructorPayload, InboundCloseNormalization) and one of the three properties (ClosingResolves) have an EXECUTED seeded-defect kill in this attempt. The other nine invariants and the two action properties carry declared falsification notes that were NOT executed here; their non-vacuity is asserted, not machine-confirmed.

The 168 distinct states are small because the lifecycle is short and most branches converge on the same absorbing states. A small state space is not a weak result on its own, but it does mean this model exercises far fewer interleavings than the US-006 connection model, and it says nothing about concurrency.

The authorization for this attempt extends a standing owner decision whose literal text authorized one attempt, already consumed by us007-sbx-output-live-0125. That extension is disclosed in the attempt's own authorization record and is the owner's to ratify or reject.
